title: Evolution simulation
description: Headless evolution simulation: progress, deaths, diversity, predator-prey dynamics, genes and run health. Hover the (i) of a panel for what it shows.

list.name: Extinctions
list.textFormat: Repopulated from the Hall of Fame

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: How long this simulation process has been running.

panels.title: Generation
panels.description: The deepest generation born so far: the longest chain of parent-to-child births since the founders.

panels.title: Ticks per second
panels.description: Simulation speed. One tick is one step of the world.

panels.title: Population
panels.description: Living creatures of each species right now.

panels.title: Extinctions
panels.description: How many times a species died out in the selected time range. The simulation refills it from its Hall of Fame right away.

panels.title: Last brain save
panels.description: Time since the best brain files in saved_brains/ were last overwritten by a new Hall of Fame record.

panels.title: Herbivore scores
panels.description: Score of the living herbivores: the best one, the mean and the median. When only the best rises, one lucky creature carries the chart; when the mean and median follow, the whole population improves.

panels.title: Carnivore scores
panels.description: Score of the living carnivores: the best one, the mean and the median. When only the best rises, one lucky creature carries the chart; when the mean and median follow, the whole population improves.

panels.title: Hall of Fame vs saved brain
panels.description: Solid: the Hall of Fame best score (the best creature that ever died, fading with HOF_SCORE_HALF_LIFE so old luck expires). Dashed: the score of the brain last written to saved_brains/. A new record above the dashed line is what gets saved next.

panels.title: Mean lifespan at death
panels.description: Average age, in ticks, of the creatures that died in the last 5 minutes. For herbivores this is the cleanest single sign of fitness: they live longer once they find food and avoid carnivores.

panels.title: Generations per hour
panels.description: How fast new generations are born. A drop means creatures breed later or less often.

panels.title: Herbivore deaths by cause
panels.description: Deaths per minute, stacked by likely cause. bitten: died in the tick a carnivore bit it. retaliation: a carnivore killed by large prey fighting back. starved: hunger past HUNGER_MAX. old_age: older than its lifespan gene. attrition: everything else (upkeep, running, signalling, hitting walls and rocks). A shift from starved to old_age means the species learned to eat.

panels.title: Carnivore deaths by cause
panels.description: Deaths per minute, stacked by likely cause. bitten: died in the tick a carnivore bit it. retaliation: a carnivore killed by large prey fighting back. starved: hunger past HUNGER_MAX. old_age: older than its lifespan gene. attrition: everything else (upkeep, running, signalling, hitting walls and rocks). A shift from starved to old_age means the species learned to eat.

panels.title: Births vs deaths
panels.description: Births (solid) and deaths (dashed) per minute. A species grows while its births are above its deaths.

panels.title: Extinctions
panels.description: Extinctions per 10 minutes. Each one wipes out the living population, which restarts from Hall of Fame elites and random brains.

panels.title: Live lineages
panels.description: Founder families still alive: every creature inherits the founder id of its first parent. When this falls to 1, one family has taken over, and evolution often plateaus soon after.

panels.title: Genetic diversity
panels.description: RMS genetic distance between two random members of the species, with genes scaled by their allowed range. The dashed line is SPECIATION_DISTANCE: pairs farther apart than that cannot breed. A collapse toward 0 means the population converged on one genome.

panels.title: Populations and food
panels.description: Living herbivores and carnivores, with food items on the right axis. Predator and prey numbers tend to chase each other in cycles: carnivores boom after herbivores do, then herbivores recover.

panels.title: Season and daylight
panels.description: Season runs from -1 (midwinter) to 1 (midsummer) and scales how much food grows. Daylight runs from 0 (night) to 1 (day); at night vision is shorter.

panels.title: Hunt success
panels.description: Herbivores killed by a bite divided by bites landed, over 5 minutes. Prey usually takes several bites to kill, so this rises as carnivores pick weaker prey or bite harder.

panels.title: Bites
panels.description: Carnivore bites that landed, per minute.

panels.title: Carcasses
panels.description: Carcasses removed per minute: eaten to the bone by scavenging carnivores, or rotted away untouched.

panels.title: Plant food
panels.description: Plant food removed per minute: eaten by herbivores, or rotted uneaten. A lot of rot means food is not what limits the herbivores.

panels.title: Herbivore gene drift
panels.description: Population mean of each herbivore gene divided by the species default, so 1 is the starting genome. 1.5 means the gene evolved 50% above its default. color is a neutral gene and is left out.

panels.title: Carnivore gene drift
panels.description: Population mean of each carnivore gene divided by the species default, so 1 is the starting genome. 1.5 means the gene evolved 50% above its default. color is a neutral gene and is left out.

panels.title: Best herbivore genes
panels.description: Raw gene values of the living herbivore with the highest score. It changes whenever another creature takes the lead.

panels.title: Best carnivore genes
panels.description: Raw gene values of the living carnivore with the highest score. It changes whenever another creature takes the lead.

panels.title: Condition
panels.description: Mean health, stamina and fat of each species, each as a share of its maximum. Fat is stored from food eaten at full health.

panels.title: Activity
panels.description: Share of each species that is swimming in a lake, standing still to eat, or winded (out of stamina and slowed down). A rising swim share in herbivores can mean they use lakes as a refuge.

panels.title: Signalling
panels.description: Mean signal output (0 to 1). Kin within SIGNAL_RADIUS hear it, and it costs health, so a rising signal means it pays off: they evolved to communicate.

panels.title: Ticks per second
panels.description: Simulation speed. It falls as populations grow, since perception and brains run for every creature each tick.

panels.title: Brain saves
panels.description: New Hall of Fame brains written to saved_brains/ per 10 minutes, at most one per AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL ticks.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the simulation process, in cores.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the simulation process.

panels.title: Brain topology
panels.description: Neurons per layer of every creature's brain, from the inputs (perception) to the outputs (rotation, speed, signal, memory).
